headline: Office of PSA convenes first ‘State Governments Nodal Officers Meeting’ to strengthen state-level coordination for wider access to Scientific and R&D infrastructure
fullText:
Office of Principal Scientific Advisor to GoI

Office of PSA convenes first ‘State Governments Nodal Officers Meeting’ to strengthen state-level coordination for wider access to Scientific and R&D infrastructure

I-STEM opens pathways for State Universities, institutions and R&D facilities to connect with the National Scientific Ecosystem

I-STEM expands State-level reach with 31,000+ scientific instruments and 4,000 institutions

21 SEP 2026 9:17PM by PIB Delhi

Dr. (Mrs.) Parvinder Maini, Scientific Secretary, Office of PSA to the Government of India chaired the first “State Governments Nodal Officers Meeting” for the I-STEM Portal on 21st September 2026. The meeting focused on strengthening the participation of State Governments in the I-STEM ecosystem and facilitating the onboarding and effective utilisation of publicly funded scientific infrastructure across States.

I-STEM was conceived and supported by the Office of the PSA and launched by the Hon’ble Prime Minister in January 2020. The platform has expanded into a national resource with more than 31,000 scientific instruments across nearly 4,000 institutions and over 65,000 registered users. By improving the utilisation of existing infrastructure, reducing duplication of investments and facilitating access to specialised facilities, I-STEM is strengthening the research and innovation ecosystem across the country. Also, the listing of publicly funded equipment costing above ₹20 lakh on I-STEM, further strengthens the framework for shared access and optimal utilisation of scientific infrastructure.

The meeting brought together State Government Nodal Officers from 23 States and 4 UTs, along with representatives from the Office of the PSA and I-STEM, to discuss mechanisms for integrating State-level universities, research institutions, laboratories and other R&D facilities with the national I-STEM platform. The meeting included an overview of I-STEM, a detailed orientation on the platform, and an interactive discussion with the Nodal Officers.

In her keynote address, Dr. (Mrs.) Parvinder Maini, Scientific Secretary, Office of PSA, highlighted the need to ensure that India’s investments in scientific and R&D infrastructure are discoverable, accessible and optimally utilised. She emphasised the role of Nodal Officers in facilitating institutional onboarding, equipment listing, wider access and effective utilisation of facilities, while addressing practical issues related to coordination and implementation. She also highlighted the importance of initiatives such as One Nation One Subscription (ONOS) in enabling wider access to high-quality scholarly resources and strengthening the research ecosystem. She further underscored that the larger objective should be to ensure that scientific infrastructure and knowledge resources created through public investment are accessible to the wider R&D and innovation ecosystem and deliver greater value to the country.

Dr. Vishal Choudhary, Scientist ‘F’, Office of PSA, provided an overview of the I-STEM Portal, while Dr. Harilal Bhaskar, COO/National Coordinator, I-STEM, conducted the detailed orientation on the platform and its functionalities. The orientation covered the process of onboarding institutions, listing scientific equipment and enabling wider access to publicly funded R&D infrastructure.

The meeting also highlighted the importance of I-STEM for State universities, colleges, technical institutions and emerging innovation ecosystems, particularly where access to specialised scientific infrastructure may be limited. It was also emphasized that all other existing similar portals (like ANALYTICS portal of CSIR) are being integrated with I-STEM through API linkages.

The deliberations and stakeholder interventions underscored the following key priorities:

Strengthening institutional onboarding: Encouraging universities, research institutions and R&D laboratories under State Governments to register on I-STEM as both users and facility providers.

Expanding access: Enabling researchers, startups, MSMEs and industry to discover and access specialised scientific infrastructure available across institutions and States.

Improving utilisation: Promoting wider and more efficient use of existing publicly funded scientific equipment and facilities.

Supporting infrastructure planning: Using the national infrastructure landscape available through I-STEM to inform future investments and minimise duplication.

Strengthening State-level coordination: Enabling State Government Nodal Officers to act as a link between State Governments, their institutions and the national I-STEM ecosystem, supporting onboarding, equipment listing, awareness and effective utilisation.

The meeting concluded with an emphasis on strengthening coordination between State-level R&D infrastructure and the national science, technology and innovation ecosystem. The State Government Nodal Officers were encouraged to facilitate wider adoption of I-STEM within their respective States and address practical issues relating to institutional onboarding, equipment listing, access, utilisation and coordination.

headline: CSIR-CRRI to lend scientific support and join hands with VMRDA and GVMC for better, safer roads in Visakhapatnam
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

CSIR-CRRI to lend scientific support and join hands with VMRDA and GVMC for better, safer roads in Visakhapatnam

21 SEP 2026 8:46PM by PIB Delhi

A high-level meeting convened by the Hon'ble Member of Parliament, Visakhapatnam, Shri M. Bharath Garu, was held today at the office of the Visakhapatnam Metropolitan Region Development Authority (VMRDA), Visakhapatnam, to chart a scientific road-improvement programme for the city. A senior delegation of the CSIR-Central Road Research Institute (CSIR-CRRI), New Delhi, led by its Director Dr. Ch. Ravi Sekhar, took part in the meeting along with senior officers of the city and the metropolitan region.

The meeting was attended, among others, by Shri Ketan Garg, IAS, Municipal Commissioner, Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC); Shri P. V. V. Satyanarayana Raju, Chief Engineer, GVMC; and Shri Vinay Kumar, Chief Engineer, VMRDA. From CSIR-CRRI, Dr. G. Bharat, Dr. Sampath Kumar P., Dr. P. S. Prasad and Dr.K.Ravinder presented the Institute's technologies for flexible pavements, performance evaluation of roads, subgrade improvement for weak and waterlogged ground, and urban road safety.

The interaction comes at a significant moment for the city, with GVMC supported by VMRDA having taken up a major programme for the upgradation of gravel and WBM roads to BT/CC standards and the development of end-to-end pavements with allied infrastructure across eight constituencies, covering around 228 km of roads, 34 km of central medians, over 1,550 street lights and improvement of key junctions. CSIR-CRRI’s scientific expertise is expected to strengthen the planning, quality and long-term durability of such works.

Opening the deliberations, the Hon'ble MP outlined the city's priorities, including bridge assessments, quality control on road projects, deployment of an i-RASTE-type intelligent road-safety system and a end to end pavement solution for Visakhapatnam, and structured training for contractors and engineers on various road-related aspects. He observed that Visakhapatnam, with its major port, industrial base, growing metropolitan region and long, demanding coastline, needs durable, scientifically engineered roads.

The detailed discussion identified a wide set of areas in which CSIR-CRRI would study the problems and propose solutions. These include relaying of roads through end-to-end paving, new roads and reconditioning of existing ones; scientific study and remedies for erosion of roads, urban flooding and coastal erosion; “right-to-walk” pedestrian facilities; road and road-safety audits; rationalisation of speed breakers; and a modern Road Asset Management System for the city's road network.

To place this cooperation on a firm and lasting footing, Dr. Ch. Ravi Sekhar, Director CRRI and Dr. Vinod Karar, chief scientist assured speedy execution on the modalities of the proposed Memoranda of Agreement/Understanding (MoA/MoU): one between CSIR-CRRI and GVMC and another between CSIR-CRRI and VMRDA covering the above areas of work. These agreements will allow CSIR-CRRI's seventy-five years of road-research expertise to be applied directly and impartially to the city’s roads.

The Hon'ble MP, Shri M. Bharath Garu, stressed the need for detailed planning of the proposed solutions and a clear, time-bound action plan, so that Visakhapatnam can have the best roads in the country. He suggested to study holistically for the world class infrastructure in Visakhapatnam. He urged the civic bodies and CSIR-CRRI to translate the day’s deliberations into work on the ground at the earliest.

Dr. Ch. Ravi Sekhar, Director, CSIR-CRRI, assured the gathering that the Institute is fully committed to partnering with GVMC and VMRDA, and that it will promptly follow up with nomination of nodal officers, joint site visits and identification of priority stretches.

As a first step, the CSIR-CRRI team, along with Shri Shanti Raju, Executive engineer, GVMC carried out survey of selected stretches of Visakhapatnam's roads to assess the road conditions, geometric design, road safety aspects, road signs, junction improvements, pedestrian facilities, and road distress parameters.

headline: As a follow up to Departmental Summit, DDWS Organised First Virtual Conference With States and UTs on Strengthening Skilled Rural Water Workforce Under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
fullText:
Ministry of Jal Shakti

As a follow up to Departmental Summit, DDWS Organised First Virtual Conference With States and UTs on Strengthening Skilled Rural Water Workforce Under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0

States/UTs urged to accelerate Nal Jal Mitra and Sujalam Shakti initiatives to build a professional, locally available workforce for sustainable rural water service delivery

21 SEP 2026 8:21PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, today organised the first National Virtual Conference with States and Union Territories, as a follow up to the Departmental Summit ( organized from 1-2 September 2026) to discuss the roadmap for strengthening the skilled rural water workforce required for sustainable operation and maintenance (O&M), water quality surveillance and long-term functionality of rural drinking water infrastructure under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0.

The Conference brought together representatives from State Water and Sanitation Missions, Public Health Engineering Departments, State Skill Development Missions, Rural Development Departments, Panchayati Raj Institutions, Technical Education Departments and other partner institutions working in skilling and technical education.

In his opening remarks, Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS, emphasised that the long-term success of Jal Jeevan Mission depends not only on infrastructure creation but also on the availability of trained and skilled human resources to operate, maintain and monitor rural water supply systems. He highlighted the need to establish a structured and professional ecosystem for operation and maintenance to sustain safe and reliable drinking water services in villages.

A major focus of the Conference was the rollout of the Nal Jal Mitra (NJM) programme. Participants were informed that DDWS, in collaboration with the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and NCVTE, has developed an NSQF-aligned Nal Jal Mitra qualification for rural drinking water systems. The programme aims to create a cadre of village-level multi-skilled technicians capable of undertaking routine operation, preventive maintenance and first-level repairs of rural water supply infrastructure. Covering skills related to pumps, pipelines, treatment systems, electrical installations and associated infrastructure, the programme forms a key component of DDWS's strategy to build a professional workforce for sustaining rural drinking water systems under JJM 2.0.

States and UTs were briefed on the two implementation pathways under the programme: a 510-hour Short-Term Training course for new entrants and a 120-hour Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) pathway for existing operators, plumbers, electricians, pump attendants and other personnel engaged in rural water supply systems. States were encouraged to leverage both pathways and prioritise local youth to ensure the availability of skilled resources within rural areas while creating livelihood opportunities.

Representatives from NCVTE outlined the process for adoption of approved qualifications and informed States about opportunities to become recognised Awarding Bodies for training, assessment and certification. The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship also highlighted opportunities available under PMKVY 4.0 and advised States to prepare district-based training plans through convergence with State Skill Development Missions, ITIs, Polytechnics and other Government training institutions.

The Department informed States and UTs that the expanding rural water sector is emerging as a significant source of local employment generation. Assessments indicate that more than 13 lakh personnel may be required in the coming years for operation and maintenance of rural water supply infrastructure, including technicians, operators, plumbers, electricians, pump mechanics, laboratory personnel, supervisors and water quality workers. States were advised to align skilling efforts with future workforce requirements so that investments in infrastructure also translate into sustainable livelihood opportunities for rural youth.

Smt. Swati Meena Naik, Joint Secretary, NJJM explained in detail about the rollout of Sujalam Shakti, a women-led initiative aimed at creating a trained village-level workforce for water quality surveillance, testing and basic disinfection. The initiative seeks to establish a community-based mechanism for regular monitoring of drinking water quality at the village level while strengthening women's participation in rural water governance.

She, informed participants that the programme is based on the NSQF Level-2 qualification titled “Fundamentals of Basic Water Quality Testing and Disinfection”. The initiative seeks to equip women with skills in representative water sampling, use of Field Test Kits (FTKs), basic chlorination and disinfection practices, sanitary inspections, source protection, record maintenance and digital reporting.

She informed that the first phase aims to train approximately 1.35-1.70 lakh women through convergence with State Rural Livelihood Missions, Panchayati Raj Institutions, Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs) and other training networks. States were advised to prioritise women already associated with water quality testing activities under Jal Jeevan Mission, Self-Help Group members and other community representatives.

The Conference also discussed strengthening linkages between the rural water sector and technical education. In this regard, AICTE presented progress on the development of a dedicated elective course on Water Supply Management for diploma and engineering students, with a focus on practical exposure to rural water supply systems.

IIT Kanpur highlighted the importance of integrating emerging technologies into future water-sector curricula and training programmes. Deliberations focused on the growing role of IoT-enabled monitoring systems, telemetry, SCADA, GIS applications, predictive maintenance tools, machine learning and data-driven decision-support systems in the management of water infrastructure. Participants observed that future technical education and skilling programmes should increasingly incorporate such technologies to prepare the next generation of water-sector professionals.

States and UTs were advised to undertake district-wise assessment of human resource requirements based on actual infrastructure and operational needs, including treatment plants, pumping stations, transmission systems, reservoirs, distribution networks and water quality laboratories. Such assessments will help identify workforce gaps and guide targeted skilling interventions. Following actionable points with timeline was also informed to States/UTs

States/SWSM are to take a decision on adoption of the existing Nal Jal Mitra (Jal Vitran Sanchalak) course, or development of a State-specific course, by 15th October 2026. On finalization, the proposal for the State to become an Awarding Body is to be submitted to NCVET accordingly.

SWSM may identify the SSDM, or another suitable body, as the Programme Implementing Agency (PIA) for STT and RPL under PMKVY. A meeting between SWSM and SSDM is to be convened before 5th October, at which the skilling target for the current financial year is to be finalized.

SWSM is to identify the number of candidates to be trained, with nominations routed through the Gram Panchayats.

SWSM to direct the DWSMs to identify ITIs with infrastructure as per PMKVY guidelines. DWSM shall be responsible for ground-level verification of the same. Any assistance which is needed to be provided by SSDM or identified PIA.

States are to draft the HR policy mandated under the JJM 2.0 guidelines and CIRP, in coordination with the Department of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj.

SWSM, along with DWSM, is to undertake a detailed HR assessment to identify O&M manpower gaps at the GP, block, and district levels.

States are to identify Sujalam Shakti members and ensure their registration on the GP dashboard platform.

During the Conference, several States shared their experiences and good practices. Odisha presented its initiatives in training local mechanics, Nal Jal Mitras and women engaged in water quality surveillance. Telangana showcased its asset-based methodology for estimating manpower requirements, while Jammu & Kashmir shared its workforce planning approach suited to its unique geographical conditions. Madhya Pradesh presented its strategy for leveraging State Institute of Rural Development (SIRD), Extension Training Centres and Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs) for implementation of Sujalam Shakti certification programmes. Haryana and Punjab highlighted efforts related to candidate identification, institutional convergence, certification and workforce deployment.

The Conference noted that development of a robust skilling ecosystem will not only strengthen operation and maintenance of rural water supply systems but also create sustainable livelihood opportunities in villages. A trained workforce of operators, plumbers, electricians, fitters, pump mechanics, water-quality personnel and other technical professionals will be critical for protecting investments made under Jal Jeevan Mission and ensuring long-term water security.

Reviewing the way forward, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, NJJM, called upon States and UTs to strengthen coordination among concerned departments and institutions, undertake district-wise HR mapping, identify training partners, accelerate adoption of Nal Jal Mitra and Sujalam Shakti qualifications, and establish mechanisms for deployment, remuneration and performance monitoring of trained personnel.

Concluding the Conference, Shri Soan reiterated that Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 marks a transition from infrastructure creation to sustainable service delivery, and that building a professional, certified and locally available workforce will be critical for ensuring reliable operation and maintenance of rural drinking water infrastructure and sustaining safe drinking water services for future generations. He urged States and UTs to take forward the skilling roadmap with urgency and commitment to support both rural water security and employment generation across the country.

headline: Central Bureau of Narcotics and Brahma Kumaris sign MoU to strengthen preventive drug awareness, youth empowerment and community outreach
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

Central Bureau of Narcotics and Brahma Kumaris sign MoU to strengthen preventive drug awareness, youth empowerment and community outreach

21 SEP 2026 7:52PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN), Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Government of India, and Prajapita Brahma Kumaris Ishwariya Vishwa Vidyalaya signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) at Mount Abu, Rajasthan, on September 18, 2026, to strengthen preventive drug awareness, youth empowerment and community outreach for promoting a healthy and substance-free society.

The initiative is in furtherance of the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for a Nasha Mukt Bharat (Drug-Free India) and seeks to contribute to the objectives of the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan through sustained preventive awareness, youth engagement and community participation.

Representatives of the Central Bureau of Narcotics and Brahma Kumaris with the signed MoU at Mount Abu.

The MoU was signed by Shri Naresh Bundel, Deputy Narcotics Commissioner, Central Bureau of Narcotics, and Dr. Banarsilal Sah, Secretary, Medical Wing, Brahma Kumaris, in the presence of Dr. Dinesh Kumar Bisen, Narcotics Commissioner, Central Bureau of Narcotics, Gwalior.

MoU signing ceremony between the Central Bureau of Narcotics and Brahma Kumaris at Mount Abu on September 18, 2026.

The MoU provides a cooperative framework for conceptualising, organising, implementing and evaluating preventive drug-awareness campaigns, youth-empowerment initiatives and community outreach programmes, with operational emphasis on Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Delhi. The collaboration focuses on value-based preventive education, awareness of the harmful effects of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, and information on counselling, recovery and treatment avenues available to persons affected by substance abuse.

Under the MoU, the Parties will support seminars, symposiums, interactive workshops, multimedia exhibitions, awareness rallies, poster-design competitions and digital awareness activities under CBN's Yuva Raksha initiative. Special attention is envisaged for schools, colleges, universities, hostels, coaching hubs and vocational training institutes, along with rural communities and youth in agricultural and traditional cultivation areas.

The partnership also provides for life-skills, stress-management and holistic-wellness activities, including meditation, yogic breathing, positive thinking and emotional self-regulation. Brahma Kumaris will support the programme through its centres, seminar venues, volunteers, instructors and spiritual counsellors, and will promote the Yuva Raksha campaign through its institutional and digital platforms.

Dr. Dinesh Kumar Bisen, Narcotics Commissioner, Central Bureau of Narcotics, addressing the gathering at Mount Abu.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Dinesh Kumar Bisen, Narcotics Commissioner, Central Bureau of Narcotics, emphasised the importance of collective and community-based efforts in preventing substance abuse. He said that sustained engagement with young people, educational institutions and communities is essential for preventive awareness. He also shared information about “Operation Yuva Raksha”, the CBN initiative for preventive awareness and youth engagement. He explained that under the initiative, awareness is taken to schools, colleges, coaching hubs and other youth-oriented platforms through seminars, symposiums, interactive sessions, awareness rallies, poster-design competitions and digital campaigns. He also highlighted the importance of developing students and young professionals as volunteer ambassadors and peer educators under the Yuva Raksha framework.

Personnel participating in the awareness and community outreach initiative at Mount Abu.

Representatives of Brahma Kumaris highlighted the role of value-based education, self-awareness, positive thinking, Rajyoga meditation, stress management and emotional wellness in supporting healthy and drug-free lifestyles. The organisation will also mobilise its youth wings, students, teachers, women's forums and community leaders to participate in awareness activities.

The MoU also provides for rural outreach, national and international anti-drug observances, volunteer orientation and capacity-building. Activities will remain voluntary, educational, inclusive and non-regulatory; participants from Brahma Kumaris will undertake awareness, educational, motivational and community-support activities and will not perform enforcement, investigation or policing functions.

The MoU marks a collaborative effort to combine the statutory expertise and preventive-awareness role of the Central Bureau of Narcotics with the extensive community network, volunteer strength and socio-spiritual outreach of Brahma Kumaris to strengthen sustained public awareness and youth participation against substance abuse.

headline: Appeal to Employees of Public Sector Banks and Regional Rural Banks for Ensuring Uninterrupted Banking Services
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

Appeal to Employees of Public Sector Banks and Regional Rural Banks for Ensuring Uninterrupted Banking Services

21 SEP 2026 7:50PM by PIB Delhi

The United Forum of Bank Unions and certain other Unions/Associations in the Public Sector Banks (supported by Regional Rural Banks) have called for a series of strikes in support of two principal demands: implementation of five-day banking, and withdrawal of the Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme. Taking due note of the concerns raised, the Government, after detailed discussion, decided to keep the PLI scheme in abeyance. This proactive initiative by the Government fulfilled one of the two main demands of the Unions.

Following this, the Government held several rounds of conciliation to address the outstanding issues through dialogue, in keeping with the established practice of resolving differences bilaterally. Despite the Government having resolved one of the two major demands of the union, and sustained conciliatory engagement, a one-day strike was held on 11.09.2026, with a further three-day strike now scheduled from 28.09.2026 to 30.09.2026, and an indefinite strike proposed from 26.10.2026, on the single demand of a five-day workweek for banks.

Public Sector Banks play a vital role in the country's economic and social development. They have been at the forefront of financial inclusion, digital banking, financial literacy and rural outreach, ensuring that formal financial services reach every section of society. Recognising this role, and acknowledging that a motivated, secure and efficient workforce is essential for a strong banking system, the Government has taken several measures aimed at improving the working environment, transparency, and welfare of bank employees. Major highlights of these initiatives are as under:

Increase in salary and allowances along with fixation of new pay scales for all cadres.

Staff Welfare Fund (SWF), a fund allocated by the PSBs for welfare-related activities (health-related expenses, subsidies on canteen, sports and cultural activities, education-related financial assistance, etc.) for working and retired officials of PSBs, was enhanced by 56% in August 2024.

The number of executive posts at the levels of Assistant General Manager, Deputy General Manager, General Manager and Chief General Manager were increased.

Recruitment of bank employees increased significantly; from FY 2014-15 to FY 2025-26, PSBs recruited ~4,82,800 employees; recruitment doubled in the last three years. As of 01.07.2026, 95.84% of Officers are in position, and 92% of Subordinate/ Award staff are in position.

Banking recruitment strengthened with the introduction of Aadhaar authentication and declaration of recruitment results streamlined to reduce attrition in banking recruitment

Promotion processes streamlined to ensure timely promotions.

Transfer policies improved to enable automated and timely transfers by developing online platforms with the provision to give location preference in case of transfers/promotions.

Special leave approved for women employees, including those related to leave during the menstrual period, infertility treatment, adoption of a second child and the events of stillbirth.

Family Pension for bank retirees revised, and Pension option granted to Resignees

A monthly Ex-gratia amount to pensioners and family pensioners for the current bipartite period has been introduced and Ex-gratia for pre-1986 retirees and their families has been increased.

Revised medical insurance policy introduced for retirees with Base policy concept.

Conveyance Allowance for PwBD employees increased

Reduction in time taken for completion of wage settlement

Further, to ensure prompt implementation of Wage Settlements and timely revision of bankers' salaries and allowances, the Government, for the first time, has begun negotiations for the upcoming Bipartite Settlement, aiming to complete it well in advance of the November 2027 deadline. These initiatives reflect the Government's continued commitment towards addressing the genuine concerns and welfare of bank employees, while strengthening the institutional framework and ensuring that the banking sector continues to function efficiently and effectively. Further, these measures indicate that the Government has already addressed the concerns of a substantial majority of bank employees over recent years.

Banking as a service is relied upon by every citizen, and its continuity directly affects the everyday lives of the general public. It may be recalled that, in the interests of bank employees, the Government declared the 2nd and 4th Saturdays of every month as public holidays for Public Sector Banks in 2015. The remaining Saturdays continue to serve as an important opportunity for many citizens to access banking services easily.

The proposed 3-day strike period, from 28th to 30th Sept 2026, also coincides with the half-yearly closing of banks on 30th September, a date of particular significance for reconciliation, provisioning, and treasury and market operations. A disruption of this nature, combined with the preceding weekend, would result in an effective five-day closure of banking services at a particularly sensitive point in the financial calendar — causing considerable inconvenience to customers, businesses, Government transactions, and international banking operations.

Public Sector Banks today stand on a healthy and robust footing — a position achieved through the sustained efforts of the Government and active contribution of bankers and bank managements over the years. It is necessary to preserve and build on this success, in the collective interest of banks, their employees, and the citizens they serve. Strikes, or disruption of work in any form, will adversely affect the banks.

Strikes cause disruption in banking services that inconvenience the public, impact the business of the bank, and ultimately harm the interests of bank employees. There is no fruitful outcome that is achieved through strikes. The Government remains committed to the welfare and well-being of bank employees and to addressing their genuine concerns through constructive engagement.

Given that most concerns of the Unions have been substantially addressed, that the remaining demand continues to be examined, and that the Government continues to proactively introduce welfare measures for the banking workforce, bank employees are urged to refrain from resorting to strikes, work towards resolving issues through dialogue, and ensure that banking services remain uninterrupted.

headline: DRI seizes over 845 kg contraband drugs at various locations in intensified crackdown on drug trafficking;
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

DRI seizes over 845 kg contraband drugs at various locations in intensified crackdown on drug trafficking;

Significant quantities of ganja, charas, cocaine and amphetamine seized; 15 persons arrested

21 SEP 2026 7:44PM by PIB Delhi

Continuing its sustained crackdown on illicit drug trafficking, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), has effected significant seizures of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances in multiple intelligence-led operations across the country. Over 845 kg contraband, including ganja/cannabis, charas, Amphetamine has been seized and 15 persons have been arrested under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985.

Seizure of charas and cannabis

On 20.09.2026, based on specific intelligence regarding smuggling of Charas/Hashish from Nepal, DRI officers intercepted two female passengers travelling by Jan Nayak Express at Gorakhpur Railway Station. Their personal search resulted in the recovery of around 6 kg of Charas/Hashish, concealed in knee caps wrapped around their thighs and hidden under their sarees. The contraband was seized and both passengers were arrested under the NDPS Act, 1985.

In addition, DRI officers also seized around 801 kg cannabis in two significant operations. On 17.09.2026, in an intelligence led operation, DRI officers intercepted a container truck near Jindapur Toll Plaza, Bodh Gaya. Search of the vehicle resulted in the recovery of around 752.3 kg ganja/cannabis, packed in 737 packets and concealed in rice husk. The contraband, vehicle and rice husk were seized and the driver was arrested.

On 11.09.2026, DRI, in coordination with the Ghariyaband Forest Department, intercepted two persons at Mentri village in Odisha, who were allegedly proceeding to deliver narcotic drugs. Search resulted in the recovery of around 48.5 kg of Ganja, packed in 25 packets in 3 sacks along with the scooter used for transportation. The contraband and vehicle were seized and both persons were arrested.

In addition, based on intelligence shared by DRI, Customs authorities at Mumbai and Bengaluru international airports seized approximately 28 kg high-grade cannabis/hydroponic weed from four passengers arriving from Thailand and Vietnam. The contraband was seized under the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985, and all four passengers were arrested.

Seizure of cocaine

In another major intelligence led operation at IGI Airport, New Delhi, on 15.09.2026, DRI officers intercepted an Indian passenger arriving from Dubai via Doha. Detailed examination of his checked-in baggage resulted in the recovery of around 5.8 kg white-coloured powder packed in nine packets, which tested positive for Cocaine during field testing. The contraband was seized and the passenger was arrested under the NDPS Act, 1985.

Seizure of Amphetamine

In series of operations, DRI intercepted multiple consignments of Amphetamine and seized cumulativelyaround 4.5 kgs of Amphetamine type stimulants and a total of five persons were arrested in these three operations.

At Mumbai, on 16.09.2026, an Indian woman passenger travelling from Delhi was intercepted and around 493 grams pills concealed inside bottles marked as Baby Powder were recovered; the pills tested positive for Amphetamine/Ecstasy. The suspected pills were seized and the passenger was arrested.

At Calicut Airport, on 09.09.2026, around 1.9 kg of Amphetamine was recovered from a passenger's baggage and a subsequent operation resulted in the arrest of the receiver and organiser, with an additional 17 grams Amphetamine and Rs. 3.45 lakh in cash recovered from their possession/vehicle.

At Indore, on the same date, DRI officers intercepted a passenger travelling by bus from Delhi and recovered around 2 kg Amphetamine, concealed inside salwar suit sets. The contraband was seized and person was arrested.

These operations underscore DRI's continued focus on disrupting organised drug-trafficking networks, intercepting narcotic consignments at different stages of their movement and detecting innovative methods of concealment.

headline: Union Minister Shri G. Kishan Reddy Calls for Stronger Recycling, Innovation and Jan Bhagidari for Critical Minerals Security
fullText:

Union Minister Shri G. Kishan Reddy Calls for Stronger Recycling, Innovation and Jan Bhagidari for Critical Minerals Security

21 SEP 2026 7:24PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Coal and Mines, Shri G. Kishan Reddy, today inaugurated the National Seminar on “India’s Critical Minerals Recycling Ecosystem and Circular Economy”, organised by the Ministry of Mines, Government of India, in collaboration with the Materials Recycling Association of India (MRAI), at Hyatt Regency, New Delhi.

The day-long seminar brought together policymakers, industry leaders, recyclers, experts, researchers, academia and other stakeholders to deliberate on strengthening India’s critical minerals recycling ecosystem and advancing a circular economy.

In his keynote address, Shri G. Kishan Reddy highlighted the strategic importance of critical minerals recycling for India’s clean energy transition, defence preparedness, digital economy and advanced manufacturing. He called for greater collaboration among government, industry, research institutions and startups to promote the recovery of critical minerals from End-of-Life (EOL) products and strengthen domestic recycling capabilities.

The Minister emphasised the need for innovative technologies, entrepreneurship, responsible e-waste management and environmental sustainability. Underscoring the importance of Jan Bhagidari, he urged citizens to view e-waste and EOL products as valuable resources for critical mineral recovery. He also called upon industry, companies and researchers to share ideas and work collectively towards a technology-driven and sustainable recycling ecosystem in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat.

Minister of State for Coal and Mines, Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, highlighted the importance of strengthening critical minerals recovery and recycling capabilities to promote resource efficiency and build a circular and self-reliant ecosystem. He stressed the need to take awareness on responsible waste management and e-waste recycling to the grassroots through wider public participation and village-to-village outreach, ensuring that recyclable resources are channelled into the formal recycling ecosystem.

Secretary, Ministry of Mines, Shri Keshav Chandra, underlined the strategic importance of critical minerals for clean energy technologies, advanced manufacturing, electronics, defence and other strategic sectors. He emphasised the need for a robust domestic ecosystem covering exploration, processing, recovery and recycling.

Shri Keshav Chandra noted that e-waste, industrial waste and other EOL materials can serve as important secondary sources for recovering critical minerals, thereby improving resource efficiency, reducing dependence on primary sources and supporting a circular economy. He called for coordinated and time-bound action by stakeholders, with clear responsibilities and defined timelines, to strengthen India’s critical mineral security.

During the seminar, the Union MinisterS also launched the Concept Paper on Critical Mineral Recycling Ecosystem, which outlines a strategic framework for strengthening critical mineral recycling in India, with a focus on resource efficiency, recovery from secondary sources and development of a circular and self-reliant ecosystem.

The seminar featured technical sessions on critical mineral recycling and e-waste collection; lithium-ion battery metal recovery and export of black mass; non-ferrous metals recycling; and the critical minerals and non-ferrous metals recycling landscape. The discussions covered technological advancements, R&D, e-waste collection, recovery of critical minerals from lithium-ion batteries and other EOL materials, black mass processing, and policy measures for strengthening the recycling sector.

The Ministry of Mines is also giving focused attention to responsible e-waste management and recycling as part of its broader efforts towards sustainable resource use. In the context of Special Campaign 6.0 and Swachhata Hi Seva, the Ministry is promoting awareness, responsible disposal and channelisation of e-waste into the formal recycling ecosystem. These efforts complement the Ministry’s broader focus on circular economy, resource efficiency and sustainable management of valuable materials, including critical minerals.

headline: Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia to convene Investors’ Meet in Bengaluru along with Chief Minister, Madhya Pradesh, Dr. Mohan Yadav to attract Investment for Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior
fullText:
Ministry of Communications

Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia to convene Investors’ Meet in Bengaluru along with Chief Minister, Madhya Pradesh, Dr. Mohan Yadav to attract Investment for Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior

Bengaluru Engagement to Strengthen Industry Participation in Telecom Manufacturing Zone, Gwalior

Asia’s First Telecom Manufacturing Zone Seeks to Accelerate Investment, Innovation and Employment; Bengaluru Engagement to Deepen Industry Participation

21 SEP 2026 7:02PM by PIB Delhi

Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, is organising an Investors’ Meet in Bengaluru, under the leadership of Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, along with Dr. Mohan Yadav, Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh to further strengthen industry participation and attract investment in Asia’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) being established in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh. The engagement builds on the strong investment momentum generated through investor engagements held in New Delhi and Mumbai.

The Bengaluru Investors’ Meet will bring together leading telecom manufacturers, technology companies, electronics and component manufacturers, investors, infrastructure providers and other key stakeholders from across the telecom ecosystem. The engagement will focus on unlocking investment opportunities, strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities, promoting innovation and creating a globally competitive telecom manufacturing ecosystem in the country. A very attractive incentive package has been announced to encourage investment under TMZ to boost India’s share in Telecom manufacturing. The package has been designed with inputs of industry.

The Bengaluru Investors’ Meet follows the successful investor engagements held in New Delhi and Mumbai. The Investors’ Roundtable meets in New Delhi and Mumbai have resulted in investment commitments of ₹5,500 crore with the potential to generate nearly 18,000 employment opportunities.

The Bengaluru engagement is expected to further build on this investment momentum by connecting the TMZ initiative with the city’s strong technology, electronics, telecom and innovation ecosystem. The interaction will provide an opportunity for industry leaders and investors to explore opportunities for manufacturing, research and development, technology partnerships, supply-chain integration and employment generation through the Telecom Manufacturing Zone.

The establishment of the Telecom Manufacturing Zone is a significant step towards advancing the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat in the telecommunications sector. The initiative seeks to strengthen domestic value chains, reduce import dependence, promote indigenous design and manufacturing, boost exports and position India as a trusted global hub for telecom products and next-generation technologies.

The Government has set an ambitious vision of transforming India from a telecom service provider into a global telecom product manufacturing and innovation hub. The Bengaluru engagement marks another important step towards translating this vision into concrete investments, manufacturing capacity, technological innovation and employment opportunities.

About Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ), Gwalior

The proposed Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior is envisaged as an integrated 170-acre plug-and-play industrial cluster for telecom manufacturing, R&D and innovation, covering mobile devices, optical fibre, telecom equipment and next-generation 5G/6G technologies. Under the recently signed MoU, the Central Government is providing 100% funding support of ₹493 crore for Phase-I, while the Government of Madhya Pradesh has provided approximately 170 acres of land free of cost along with various investor incentives.

The Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) has been established for this purpose with a 51% equity from the Government of Madhya Pradesh and 49% from the Department of Telecommunications.

headline: India-New Zealand FTA to Enter into Force from 20 October 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

India-New Zealand FTA to Enter into Force from 20 October 2026

Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Says India-New Zealand FTA Will Give Fresh Momentum to Bilateral Trade, Technology and Investment Ties

Zero Duty on 100% of India’s Exports to New Zealand from Day One

Gains from Farms to Factories as Textiles, Leather, Footwear, Engineering Goods and Agri-Processing Enter New Zealand Duty Free

New Horizons for India’s Youth, Women, Farmers and MSMEs as Jobs, Investment and Mobility Get a Boost

21 SEP 2026 7:01PM by PIB Delhi

In a defining step forward for trade and economic partnership, the India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement, is going to enter into force on 20th October 2026. The FTA was signed on 27th April 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, by Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and New Zealand’s Minister for Trade and Investment Hon. Todd McClay.

Today, the Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and New Zealand’s Minister for Trade and Investment Hon. Todd McClay spoke via virtual conference and announced the date for entering into force of the agreement following the completion of internal processes in both countries. The legislation was passed by the New Zealand Parliament on 16th September, 2026.

Under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India and New Zealand have continued to deepen and expand their engagement. The visit of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji to New Zealand in July 2026, the first visit by an Indian Prime Minister to New Zealand in four decades, provided further momentum to the bilateral relationship and emphasised the importance of the early implementation of the India-New Zealand FTA. The visit also marked an important elevation in the relationship, with India and New Zealand announcing a Strategic Partnership and endorsing the India-New Zealand Strategic Partnership: Roadmap to 2030 as a shared framework to guide cooperation over the next four years including an aspirational goal of doubling bilateral two-way trade in goods and services to NZ$7 billion (approximately ₹35,000 crore) by 2030. Operationalisation of the FTA will serve as a key enabler for translating the ambitions of the Strategic Partnership: Roadmap to 2030 into tangible economic outcomes.

Highlighting the significance of the milestone, the Hon’ble Commerce & Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal said “ The India-New Zealand FTA would provide fresh momentum to the bilateral partnership, create greater synergies between the two economies, enable economies of scale and contribute to enhancing overall competitiveness”. Emphasising the symbolism of the chosen date, he said, “We have chosen the auspicious day Dussshera- Vijay Dashmi for the entry into force of the India-New Zealand FTA. I am confident that the entry into force will overcome all hurdles that stood between our trade, technology and investment relationship, and will ensure prosperity for people of both sides”.

Hon. Todd McClay, Minister for Trade and Investment, noted that at a time of uncertainty in trade and rising tariffs, India New Zealand FTA gives confidence. With hard work, we have delivered one of the highest quality agreements concluded in nine months, which will provide tangible benefits to businesses and stakeholders on both sides. He highlighted that the Agreement is a great foundation for both Governments to cooperate in greater areas, be it people-to-people cooperation, culture, sports, business or investment and we will work together to address challenges faced by businesses to create greater employment opportunities on both sides.

From the entry into force, every single tariff line covering 100% of India's exports to New Zealand becomes duty-free, offering Indian industry a level playing field that puts it on par with New Zealand's other trading partners. Sectors that power livelihoods across the country - textiles and apparel, leather and footwear, gems and jewellery, engineering goods and processed foods - stand to gain immediately as New Zealand's peak tariffs of up to 10% are eliminated. Indian manufacturers will also benefit from tariff-free access to critical inputs such as wooden logs, coking coal and metal scrap, sharpening their competitive edge in global markets.

At the same time, the Government has safeguarded the interests of Indian farmers by keeping sensitive products such as dairy, animal meat (except sheep), key agricultural commodities, sugar and edible oils excluded from tariff concessions. A calibrated market access has been structured for New Zealand’s apples, kiwifruit and Manuka honey through Tariff Rate Quotas with Minimum Import Price and seasonal import windows, alongside safeguards to protect domestic farmers. The Agreement establishes an Agriculture Productivity Partnership to strengthen cooperation in agriculture, with dedicated Action Plans for kiwifruit, apples and honey aimed at improving productivity, quality and farmer incomes in India. Centres of Excellence will be established for orchard management, post-harvest practices, supply chains, food safety and sustainable beekeeping, facilitating the exchange of knowledge, technology and capacity. A Joint Agriculture Productivity Council will monitor that the market access is complemented by cooperation activities by New Zealand under Agriculture Productivity Partnership.

The FTA also sets the stage for deeper investment gains for India, with New Zealand's commitment to facilitate USD 20 billion in investment into India. This investment by New Zealand will benefit Indian agriculture, manufacturing, infrastructure and start-ups.

For India's rapidly growing services sector, the Agreement creates a stronger platform for Indian companies and professionals to access the New Zealand market and expand their international footprint spanning roughly 118 sectors including IT, professional services, audio-visual, construction and tourism, with Most-Favoured Nation treatment locked in across about 139 sub-sectors, mobility opportunity through a dedicated quota of 5,000 Temporary Employment Entry visas for skilled Indians and 1,000 Working Holiday visas each year for young Indians. The agreement also provides uncapped student mobility with post-study work rights of up to three years for STEM graduates and four years for doctoral scholars.

India's pharmaceutical and medical device exporters gain a long-awaited edge as New Zealand begins accepting inspection approvals from globally trusted regulators such as the US FDA, EMA, UK MHRA and Health Canada, cutting long waiting time and speeding up market entry.

With bilateral merchandise trade already at around USD 1.1 billion in 2025-26, the entry into force of the India-New Zealand FTA is set to give a decisive push to two-way trade, investment and job creation in the years ahead. Anchored in the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047, the Agreement stands as another testament to India's growing network of partnerships with developed economies - one that places farmers, women, youth, artisans and MSMEs at the very heart of its gains.

headline: Gujarat’s Cultural Heritage and Contemporary Achievements Features in PM Mementos e-Auction 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Culture

Gujarat’s Cultural Heritage and Contemporary Achievements Features in PM Mementos e-Auction 2026

Traditional crafts, architectural heritage and modern innovations from Gujarat find a place in the 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction

21 SEP 2026 6:44PM by PIB Delhi

The 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026 showcases a diverse collection of mementos from Gujarat, reflecting the state’s rich cultural heritage, traditional arts and crafts, architectural legacy, textiles and contemporary achievements. The collection brings together distinctive representations of Gujarat’s cultural identity, highlighting its enduring traditions alongside its contributions to modern India.

Gujarat’s Rich Cultural Legacy Meets Contemporary India

The Gujarat collection features mementos representing the state’s architectural heritage, traditional textile arts, indigenous painting traditions, sporting achievements and technological progress.

An architectural representation of the 17th-century Hatkeshwar Mahadev Temple Memento, Vadnagar, featuring its distinctive ornamentation and elements inspired by the Ramayana and Mahabharata.

A sporting memorabilia item presented by Gujarat's table tennis player Manav Thakkar, who has represented India at international competitions including the Commonwealth Games and Asian Championships.

A traditional Mata-ni-Pachedi – Tree of Life textile painting, depicting wisdom, strength, prosperity and the interconnectedness of all living beings.

Framed Pithora Painting associated with the Rathwa, Bhil and Bhilala communities of central Gujarat, featuring horses, deities and motifs representing the cultural and belief systems associated with Pithora art.

India's First Solar Tile with Engraved Glass of Modhera Sun Temple, bringing together Gujarat's heritage and India's advances in solar energy

The auction also includes other mementos representing the cultural heritage and development of Gujarat, featuring representations of the Ambaji Temple, Somnath Temple and Dwarkadhish Ji; a traditional Bhujodi shawl and Lippan art; a replica model of AIIMS Rajkot; a layered wooden architectural memento of the Adalaj Stepwell; and the Tata Electronics commemorative semiconductor plaque titled “Charkha to Chips”.

The 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction started from 17th September, 2026, offers a total of 1,498 mementos from across India, representing the country’s diverse artistic traditions, traditional craftsmanship, cultural practices, spiritual traditions and sporting achievements.

The auction is organised by the Ministry of Culture through the National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA), New Delhi, the initiative provides citizens, collectors, institutions and art enthusiasts an opportunity to acquire unique mementos presented to the Prime Minister on various occasions.

The proceeds from the PM Mementos e-Auction will support the Namami Gange Programme, the national mission dedicated to the conservation, rejuvenation and protection of the River Ganga and its ecosystem. The initiative connects India’s cultural heritage with a significant national environmental mission.

The PM Mementos e-Auction, which began in January 2019, has raised more than ₹50 crore for the Namami Gange Project through its earlier editions.

The PM Mementos e-Auction 2026 is being conducted online through the official portal: https://pmmementos.gov.in/#/

headline: Union Minister, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh and Shri Suvendu Adhikari, Hon'ble Chief Minister, West Bengal Co-Chaired Review meeting on implementation of Schemes and Programmes for development of fisheries and aquaculture in West Bengal
fullText:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

Union Minister, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh and Shri Suvendu Adhikari, Hon'ble Chief Minister, West Bengal Co-Chaired Review meeting on implementation of Schemes and Programmes for development of fisheries and aquaculture in West Bengal

Focus on charting Roadmap for Sustainable Growth of the Fisheries Sector by Enhancing Production, Strengthening Market Linkages and Fisheries Value Chain Development

21 SEP 2026 6:01PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Government of India organized a Review Meeting on Development of Fisheries and Aquaculture in West Bengal on 21st September 2026 in Kolkata, West Bengal co-chaired by Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj and Shri Suvendu Adhikari, Hon'ble Chief Minister, West Bengal. After more than a decade, a high-level fisheries review meeting was organized to chart a roadmap for realizing the untapped fisheries potential of West Bengal.

The review meeting was held in the gracious presence of Shri Rajesh Mahata, Hon'ble Minister of State (Independent Charge) Department of Fisheries & Department of Animal Resources Development, Government of West Bengal, Shri Manoj Kumar Agarwal, Hon’ble Chief Secretary, Government of West Bengal. The meeting also witnessed participation from officials from Department of Fisheries, GoI, West Bengal state fisheries department, National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB), ICAR institutes, National Bureau of Fish Genetic Resources (NBFGR), CIFE, National Bank of Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC), Indian Coast Guard, Coastal Aquaculture Authority (CAA), Export Inspection Council (EIC) and Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA).

Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj handed over the administrative approval for development of 6 Reservoirs at a cost of Rs. 832.50 lakh with central share of Rs. 499.50 lakh to Shri Suvendu Adhikari, Hon'ble Chief Minister, West Bengal.

The Union Minister highlighted West Bengal's vast untapped fisheries potential and stated that, despite being the second-largest fish-producing State, it has significant scope to increase productivity, aquaculture, exports and value addition. He noted that the State currently exports fisheries products worth about ₹5,000 crore but has the potential to increase this to ₹15,000–20,000 crore through expansion of aquaculture, He noted that Sundarbans has immense potential for aquaculture-led export growth particularly through high-value species such as black tiger shrimp, mud crab, hilsa and ornamental fish, and development of export-oriented infrastructure. Referring to the national growth of the sector, he stated that India's fish production has increased from 95.7 lakh tonnes in 2014 to 197.75 lakh tonnes, while fisheries exports have more than doubled to ₹73,890 crore. He emphasized the need to strengthen seed quality, feed, disease management, cold chain infrastructure, fishing harbours, fish landing centres and deep-sea fishing capabilities under the upcoming PMMSY 2.0 and assured the Government of India's full support in enhancing production, productivity and exports from West Bengal.

Shri Suvendu Adhikari, Chief Minister, West Bengal underscored the State's commitment to working closely with the Government of India to unlock the immense potential of the fisheries sector, particularly in North 24 Parganas, South 24 Parganas and the Sundarbans region. He highlighted the importance of flagship initiatives such as PMMSY, the National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP) and PM-MKSSY in strengthening fisheries development and improving the welfare of fishers. Stressing the need for enhanced safety and security of fishermen operating in deep-sea waters, he called for greater focus on communication systems, wireless connectivity, control room infrastructure and emergency response mechanisms. He also emphasized the importance of improving fishing harbours, cold-chain infrastructure, supply chains and coastal village development under initiatives such as Sagarmala, while assuring full cooperation between the State and Central Governments for effective implementation of fisheries schemes and maximizing benefits for the nearly 50 lakh people dependent on the sector.

Shri Rajesh Mahata, Hon'ble Minister of State (Independent Charge) Department of Fisheries & Department of Animal Resources Development, Government of West Bengal, highlighted that the State recorded a fish production of 25.43 lakh metric tonnes in 2025-26, making it the second-largest fish-producing State in the country, while also retaining its position as the leading fish seed producer. He emphasized the need to improve productivity, quality and efficiency through better seed, feed, farm management and disease control, while strengthening traceability and regulatory compliance to support exports. He noted that under PMMSY, fisheries interventions worth ₹102.23 crore of Central share and ₹66.48 crore of State share have been mobilized in the State. Stressing the importance of registration on the National Fisheries Digital Platform, cold-chain infrastructure, value addition, market linkages and fisher safety, he called for greater adoption of science and technology and reaffirmed the State Government's commitment to working closely with the Government of India and research institutions for sustainable growth of the fisheries sector.

Shri Manoj Kumar Agarwal, Hon’ble Chief Secretary, Government of West Bengal highlighted the immense untapped potential of the fisheries sector in West Bengal, observing that only a fraction of the State's potential has been harnessed so far. He emphasized the need for closer coordination between the Central and State Governments, accelerated implementation of fisheries schemes, and greater participation of fish farmers through initiatives such as the National Fisheries Digital Platform. Stressing the importance of timely execution of projects, preparation of a robust pipeline of proposals, adoption of best practices, and focused capacity building, he called for sustained institutional collaboration to maximize investments and deliver tangible outcomes for the growth of the fisheries sector and the livelihoods dependent on it.

Shri Shubhanjan Das, Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Government of West Bengal, highlighted that the fisheries sector supports the livelihoods of nearly 32 lakh people in the State. He informed that implementation of long-pending PMMSY projects, including the upgradation of fishing harbours at Fraserganj, Kakdwip, Shankarpur and Petuaghat, has been expedited and sought continued support under PMMSY Phase-II. He also outlined initiatives to expand fisher registration through the National Fisheries Digital Platform, develop reservoir fisheries in Bankura and Purulia, promote modern technologies such as biofloc, cage culture and soft-shell crab farming, and strengthen mariculture, export facilitation, aquaculture regulation and maritime safety.

Dr. Surabhi Rai, Joint Secretary (Marine), Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, presented an overview of the Department’s schemes and programmes and reviewed their implementation in West Bengal. She highlighted the State’s potential in ornamental fisheries and high-value species, while emphasizing traceability, deep-sea fishing through vessel modernization, promotion of crab culture in the Sundarbans, strengthening post-harvest infrastructure, formation of FFPOs and cooperatives, and greater focus on training, certified seed, quarantine facilities and targeted outreach of fisheries schemes.

Representatives from leading fisheries institutions highlighted a range of interventions to accelerate fisheries development in West Bengal. The Coastal Aquaculture Authority assured support for expediting farm registrations and strengthening export compliance, while ICAR-CIFA emphasized improving seed quality through broodstock management and hatchery certification, promoting indigenous ornamental fish species, and expanding culture of commercially important species to reduce imports. ICAR-CIBA highlighted the vast potential of brackish water aquaculture through diversification into mud crab, seabass, black tiger shrimp and cage culture, while ICAR-CMFRI stressed sustainable marine fisheries management, conservation of fish stocks, and promotion of mariculture, seaweed cultivation and marine ornamental fisheries. ICAR-CIFRI proposed structured training programmes for fish farmers, the Central Institute of Coldwater Fisheries Research highlighted opportunities for rainbow trout farming in Darjeeling and Kalimpong, and ICAR-NBFGR emphasized genetic resource conservation, broodstock improvement, biosecurity and disease surveillance. The institutions collectively assured scientific, technical and capacity-building support to enhance productivity, sustainability and fisheries-based livelihoods in the State.

The review meeting underscored the importance of sustained cooperation between the Government of India, the Government of West Bengal and allied institutions for accelerating the growth of the fisheries and aquaculture sector in the State. The deliberations provided a clear framework for focused action on productivity enhancement, infrastructure development, technology adoption, capacity building and improved service delivery, with a view to strengthening livelihoods and realizing the full potential of the sector in West Bengal.

headline: Sowa-Rigpa Working Group Holds First Meeting Under PCIM&H
fullText:
Sowa-Rigpa Working Group Holds First Meeting Under PCIM&H

21 SEP 2026 5:57PM by PIB Delhi

The first meeting of the Sowa-Rigpa Working Group, constituted under the Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H), was held on September 18, at PCIM&H, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh. The meeting marks an important step towards the development of Sowa-Rigpa Pharmacopoeias and Formularies in India.

The meeting was chaired by Dr. Kousthubha Upadhyaya, Director, PCIM&H. Sowa-Rigpa was represented by four experts from various Sowa-Rigpa institutions, including Dr. Padma Gurmet, Director, National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa, Leh.

Dr. Padma Gurmet expressed gratitude to the Government of India for formally initiating the work on Sowa-Rigpa Pharmacopoeias and Formularies.

The Working Group will undertake a step-wise action plan for the development of Formularies, Pharmacopoeias and other statutory and non-statutory documents required to support the implementation of regulatory provisions and quality assurance of Sowa-Rigpa drugs. The work will be undertaken within the ambit of PCIM&H and in accordance with the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the Rules thereunder.

The initiative is aimed at further development and standardisation of the Sowa-Rigpa system of medicine within the Government of India’s regulatory framework for traditional medicines. The development of Pharmacopoeias and Formularies will provide a structured basis for quality standards and regulatory requirements for Sowa-Rigpa drugs.

The Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy is a subordinate office under the Ministry of Ayush, responsible for the development of Pharmacopoeias and Formularies and functioning as the Central Drug Testing-cum-Appellate Laboratory for Indian Systems of Medicine and Homoeopathy.

headline: Dr. Jitendra Singh Applauds Mass Participation in 'Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar 5.0'; 15 Lakh People Take Ocean Conservation Pledge; Coastal cleanup conducted at 231 Locations across 13 States/UTs
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

Dr. Jitendra Singh Applauds Mass Participation in 'Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar 5.0'; 15 Lakh People Take Ocean Conservation Pledge; Coastal cleanup conducted at 231 Locations across 13 States/UTs

Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Pushes for City-Based Scientific Clusters, Stronger Synergy and Wider Public Outreach of India’s Scientific Achievements

Minister Seeks Greater Synergy Among Science Ministries and Departments to Take Scientific Achievements Closer to the People

‘Vigyan Ki Baat’ to Deepen Public Connect with Science; Second Edition on September 26 to Focus on Foundational Physical Sciences and Quantum Technology

Dr. Jitendra Singh Reviews Digital Library of Scientific Achievements, CSIR@85 and ESTIC-2026 Preparations

21 SEP 2026 5:55PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and MoS in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, today called for stronger coordination among Science Ministries and Departments, development of city-based scientific clusters and wider public outreach of India’s scientific achievements.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also reviewed the just concluded 'Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar' 5.0 and the scale of public participation generated by the campaign. Conducted from September 12 to 19, 2026, the coastal clean-up covered 231 locations across 13 States/UTs, with 15 lakh people taking the Ocean Conservation Pledge.

The Monthly Review Meeting of Scientific Ministries/Departments, chaired by Dr. Jitendra Singh, was attended by Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood; Secretary, Department of Biotechnology, Dr. Rajesh Gokhle; Secretary, Department of Science & Technology, Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare; Secretary, Department of Scientific & Industrial Research, Prof. N. Kalaiselvi; Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, Dr. T. Srinivasa Kumar; and CEO, Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF), Dr. Shivkumar Kalyanaraman, along with senior officials of the concerned Ministries, Departments and scientific institutions.

Dr. Jitendra Singh emphasised that India’s scientific institutions should work with greater synergy and visibility, with city-based scientific clusters helping bring together institutions and stakeholders working in related areas. He also called for continuous identification and showcasing of new and impactful scientific achievements, so that important work emerging from laboratories and institutions reaches a wider section of society.

The Minister called for strengthening the communication ecosystem across Science Ministries and Departments so that significant achievements in science, technology and innovation are communicated in a timely, accessible and engaging manner. The emphasis was on taking scientific achievements beyond institutional boundaries and creating a stronger connect between India’s scientific ecosystem and citizens.

The meeting reviewed progress on the proposed Digital Library of Scientific Achievements, envisaged as a common repository of videos and other communication products showcasing the work of India’s scientific institutions. CSIR-NIScPR is working as the nodal institution for developing the institutional mechanism and implementation framework for the Digital Library, while modalities for participation and resource pooling among the concerned Ministries and Departments are being worked out.

The review also took stock of the ongoing digital outreach efforts of DST, DBT, DSIR/CSIR and MoES, including the creation and dissemination of short-form content highlighting significant scientific and technological achievements. The coordinated approach is aimed at giving wider visibility to the work of scientific institutions and ensuring that important developments are communicated beyond the scientific community.

The Minister called for sustaining this momentum of public participation and strengthening the connection between scientific awareness, environmental responsibility and citizen action. The campaign brought together citizens, students, coastal communities, government agencies, scientific institutions and volunteers in a nationwide effort for cleaner coasts and safer seas.

The meeting also reviewed the progress of ‘Vigyan Ki Baat’, the monthly lecture series launched by the Department of Science & Technology to showcase the work of India’s autonomous scientific institutions and take their achievements to a wider audience. The second edition is scheduled for September 26, 2026, featuring the Director of the S.N. Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences, with the session focusing on advances in foundational physical sciences and quantum technology.

The inaugural edition of ‘Vigyan Ki Baat’, held on August 29, 2026, witnessed participation of more than 7,500 people from academia, research organisations and industry. The series is envisaged as a regular platform for communicating cutting-edge research, technological innovation and their national relevance, while strengthening the public interface of India’s scientific institutions.

The meeting also reviewed preparations for CSIR@85, including the programme scheduled for September 25, 2026, as well as updates relating to ESTIC-2026. The discussions covered programme preparedness, coordination and effective communication of the achievements and contributions of India’s scientific institutions.

The review further covered mechanisms for inter- and intra-ministerial coordination, including thematic interactions and cluster-based engagements aimed at promoting collaboration and synergies across the scientific ecosystem. Regular exchange among the communication teams of the scientific Ministries and Departments was also emphasised to facilitate coordinated outreach and wider dissemination of scientific achievements.

Dr. Jitendra Singh stressed the importance of ensuring that India’s advances in science, technology and innovation are visible, accessible and relevant to society, with stronger institutional collaboration, coordinated communication and sustained public engagement forming an integral part of the scientific ecosystem.

The meeting concluded with emphasis on taking forward these initiatives in a coordinated manner, strengthening the interface between scientific institutions and the public, and ensuring wider visibility for India’s scientific achievements and innovations.
